about: Intended differences between each instrument and the reference on the Create Chart tab, checked by tests/test_instrument_parity.py (how to read and extend it: scripts/instrument_parity.py). 'intended' entries were judged; 'known_to_review' entries were seen and recorded honestly but not judged yet. Every entry must still match what the app does, or the test fails.

shared.reason: These follow a person from one instrument to the next because they describe the person's print, not the instrument (resolution, bit depth, compression, PDF, the label and sheet-text style, the clip text), or because the new instrument does not use them and keeps them unchanged (area sizing, scales, stagger, hexagon orientation, rotations, the summary stamp).

intended.reason: "Left border" and "No strip limit" belong to the i1Pro's clip band and ruler; this instrument has neither.
The density (ColorMunki) or hexagon (SpectroScan, CR30) choice is this instrument's own; the i1Pro has none.
Triple density exists only for the ColorMunki.
Aiming crosses and the clip border of the i1iO table are its own options (Beta); the i1Pro's clip band is a different control.
Only ChromIQ's layout engine can lay out this instrument's chart (printtarg cannot), so the engine switch is on and greyed, with its reason.
The i1Pro's strip length is set by its ruler; an instrument without that ruler gets the strip-length cap open.
The CR30 starts without spacers, so their width is greyed until spacers are switched on (the spacer row beside it is the reason).
The FD-9 Beta builds its chart with its own layout and greys these options of the shared panel, each with its reason (the FD-9 is a contributed Beta: observed only, never changed here).
Options of the shared strip layout (area-first sizing, scales, mode, rotation, the summary stamp, the clip side) that the FD-9 and i1iO builders do not use; greyed with their reason.

The i1iO's table moves to every patch by its corner crosses, so its margins, edge spacers, label alignment and strip-length cap are open, where the i1Pro takes them from its instrument margins and ruler.
